BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. 1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal, privileged working draft. Not for circulation to the Seller.

## Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's note says that clauses marked [STANDARD] "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides." It also says the Buyer has "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package."

**We should not accept either statement.**
- Nothing in our playbook or authority record shows that we agreed to any of these positions.
- Under playbook §0.4/§6.3, a counterparty's statement that a term is "agreed," "standard" or "pre-cleared" is not a firm instruction.
- Every [STANDARD] item below has been reviewed in full.
- Our mark-up should say expressly that we do not accept the labels or the efficiency note. It should also record that nothing is agreed until it is agreed in the executed SPA.

The Disclosure Letter is useful, but on the Seller's own facts it contradicts several "addressed" positions in the Update (see SPA-N-008, 009, 010 and 012).

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (Cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.**
- **Reason:** 20% is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this draft, and we have none. Matching a fallback number does not clear it.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with recovery of the excess only (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000. Once the basket is exceeded, the Seller is liable from the first dollar (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** Both thresholds are five times our position, and the deductible structure removes up to AUD 250k of recovery permanently.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months (Cl 12.3/13). Its rider that "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" is dealt with under SPA-N-014.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months after Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 24 months.**
- **Reason:** 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, and none has been given.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties would sit under the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with:
  - a 100% (price) cap;
  - a claims period of at least six years;
  - no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for. "Administrative simplicity" is no justification for capping them at 20%.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clauses "to all Claims of any nature," which on its face reaches fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of the following, to the maximum extent enforceable:
  - caps;
  - baskets;
  - time limits;
  - exclusive remedy;
  - non-reliance.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express carve-out.**
- **Reason:** This is a non-waivable playbook position, and a Seller should not be able to limit liability for its own fraud.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2, Sch 7).
- **Buyer wants:** Only specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties, with enough detail for the Buyer to assess the matter.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete DL 1.1–1.2 and the matching Sch 7 language.**
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure would empty the warranties of content.
- **Also:** Keep DL 1.4 (no admission) under review so that it cannot be used to undercut the specific disclosures.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Blanket exclusion of any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, or that was discoverable from the data room or public records (Cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the clause.
- **Fallback, only if a qualifier is unavoidable:** Limit it to the *Seller's* knowledge of named persons after reasonable enquiry. It must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete Cl 8.3.**
- **Reason:** Combined with general disclosure, the "discoverable" limb would bar almost every claim, including claims under the indemnities we are negotiating for.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Described as "addressed." The Seller offers reasonable endeavours only, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of a written consent (Cl 3/6.3).
- **Facts (DL 2):** DD-002 shows Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (roughly 30%). The contract has a change-control clause (11.2) and consent conditions (11.3). No final consent or evidence that the conditions are met has been provided. "Addressed" is therefore an assertion, not a verified update.
- **Buyer wants:** A Condition Precedent to Completion requiring both:
  - an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent; and
  - evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions have been satisfied.
  The CP should be waivable by the Buyer only. Reasonable endeavours alone is not enough.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the consent-on-delivery mechanism.**
- **Reason:** A consent that is delivered but still subject to unmet conditions could leave about 30% of revenue at risk after Completion.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release "to be provided following Completion" (Cl 2/7).
- **Facts (DL 3):** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The facility contains change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. It has not been repaid and no discharge is in hand.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds;
  - executed security releases (including PPSR discharges) delivered at Completion.
- **Fallback:** A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from the bank and Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** We cannot buy on a debt-free basis while AUD 3.2m of security, plus a possible change-of-control trigger, remains live over the Company.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Facts (DL 5):** The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment. DL 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs either:
  - treated as a specific Completion deduction or debt-like item in the funds flow; or
  - funded by the Seller, backed by a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the current funds flow.**
- **Reason:** "A matter for the Seller" has no contractual effect. The liability sits in the Company we acquire, and the funds flow must not exclude it without saying so.
- **Diligence:** Confirm whether on-costs apply.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The Cl 11.1 indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is said to be "adequate."
- **Facts (DL 4):** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. The Seller accepts this is not bank-verified. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment exists.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The indemnity broadened to cover the Ironquay ownership, assignment and infringement position generally.
  - The SOW3 cure preserved: payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, ideally as a Completion deliverable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted.**
- **Reason:** The risk is that the Company does not own the Project Materials, not merely an unpaid invoice.
- **Note:** Do not treat AUD 180,000 as confirmed in either direction. Verify it independently.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" (Cl 4.6/Sch 6).
- **Facts (DL 6):** A download link was sent to an unintended external email address. About 1,240 records may be involved. Access, exact scope and any notification duty have not yet been established.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion covenants requiring the Seller to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence;
  - complete a proper investigation, including the notifiable data breach assessment under the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth);
  - give the Buyer regular written updates and access to findings;
  - not make admissions or notifications without consulting the Buyer;
  - provide a specific indemnity for any resulting loss, regulatory outcome or remediation, outside the general limitations.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation, and do not concede it in our draft either.**
- **Reason:** The facts are unresolved. We should neither accept the Seller's assurance nor assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Facts (DL 8):** The renewals appear in DD-008 and DD-011 and should be read together. DL 8 does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Diligence on:
  - timing, scope and whether the three renewals are related or split;
  - termination rights;
  - accrual status;
  - whether they were entered in the ordinary course.
  Then decide on treatment.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the Seller's characterisation. Do not automatically treat the renewals as Debt or a price deduction either.**
- **Reason:** The facts are not established. Assess them first, then reserve rights, such as an ordinary-course warranty or conduct-of-business covenant, as the findings justify.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:**
  - Cl 12.3/13: any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise."
  - Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5: limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature."
  - Title, Tax and IP are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for Title/Fundamental claims, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants, with no catch-all override from the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete the catch-all wording and draft each regime expressly.**
- **Reason:** These clauses would silently apply the 20% cap, AUD 250k basket and 18-month limit to indemnities, covenants, price obligations, title and even fraud.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the DD-012 share register.
- **Facts (DL 10):** The Seller accepts that DD-012 is only the source relied on and that the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, including:
  - a current ASIC company extract and member search;
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company (and Riverlark security; see SPA-N-009);
  - the Seller's constitution and board approvals;
  - share certificates;
  - confirmation that there are no options, pre-emption or third-party rights.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient.**
- **Reason:** A register supplied by the Seller is an internal record, not independent proof.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** The tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP treated as **OPEN** and negotiated as their own regimes, for example a tax indemnity and IP-specific warranties with their own caps and time limits.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the claim that these terms are "settled."**
- **Reason:** Nothing on our side records agreement. We should not assume unlimited liability in our favour or any resolution in the Seller's favour.

---

## Summary and next steps

1. **No playbook position has been conceded.** All 16 issues remain open despite the [STANDARD] labels. Our cover note should expressly reject the efficiency note.
2. **No fallback is available yet.** The 20% cap and 18-month period need Amelia Frost's written authority, identifying this draft. If the team wants to use them as trade-offs, seek that authority first.
3. **Completion deliverables and CPs to table:**
   - Bluefen effective consent plus evidence the conditions are satisfied;
   - Riverlark payout letter and releases at Completion;
   - Ironquay payment and confirmatory assignment;
   - independent title searches.
4. **Price mechanics:** Add the AUD 420k bonuses plus on-costs to the funds flow or cover them with a Seller indemnity. Assess Sandbar before deciding treatment.
5. **Specific protections:** DD-006 covenants and indemnity, a broadened Ironquay indemnity, and the fraud carve-out (non-negotiable).
6. **Verification tasks:** Independent check of the AUD 180k SOW3 balance, DD-006 investigation updates, the Sandbar diligence above, the bonus on-cost analysis, and title searches.

- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
